title: Personal Credit Cards: Rewards Currency, Earn Rates and Bonus Categories
content:
Four tiers of Personal Credit Cards earn rewards, either as cash back or as points; two tiers earn nothing. Each earning tier sets a base rate per whole dollar of net purchases, a higher rate for purchases in its bonus merchant categories, and a quarterly ceiling on bonus-category spending that earns the higher rate.

| Tier | Rewards currency | Base earn per whole dollar | Bonus merchant categories | Bonus earn per whole dollar | Bonus-category spending per calendar quarter that earns the bonus rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | none | 0 | none | 0 | not applicable |
| College Rewards Visa | cash back | 1 | dining, grocery | 2 | 1000.00 USD |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | none | 0 | none | 0 | not applicable |
| Cash Rewards Visa | cash back | 1.5 | grocery, gas, dining | 3 | 2500.00 USD |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | points | 1 | travel, dining | 3 | no ceiling |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | points | 1.5 | travel, dining | 3 | no ceiling |

## Basis Q&A

- **Do cash back tiers still count in points?** Yes; earnings on every earning tier are kept as a points balance, whatever the rewards currency is called.
- **What happens to bonus-category spending above the quarterly figure?** Spending beyond the ceiling in a quarter earns the base rate instead of the bonus rate; on tiers with no ceiling the bonus rate applies to all bonus-category spending.

> Hypothetical illustration: on College Rewards Visa, a 40.00 USD grocery purchase made while the quarter's grocery and dining spending is well under 1000.00 USD earns 2 points per whole dollar, or 80 points; a 40.00 USD streaming purchase earns the base 1 point per dollar, or 40 points.
